headline: All three segments grow, margins expand, guidance raised
summary_short: L3Harris reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.881 billion, up 8.4% y/y and 2.4% q/q, with net income of $600 million (+31.0% y/y) and diluted EPS of $3.13 (+28.3% y/y); the company also raised full-year 2026 revenue and EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue grew 8.4% y/y to $5.881B on growth across all segments — new program starts and execution against a record $42B backlog. Operating margin expanded 60bps to 11.1% as higher Communications & Spectrum Dominance segment income and lower corporate expense offset the absence of a prior-year $92M asset-sale gain. Diluted EPS rose 28% to $3.13. Free cash flow was $771M, up 37% y/y. L3Harris raised FY2026 guidance: revenue to $23.2-23.7B (from $23.0-23.5B) and diluted EPS to $11.80-12.00 (from $11.40-11.60). Cash rose to $1.521B, boosted by a $973M subsidiary preferred-stock issuance; long-term debt fell 16.3% y/y to $9.184B.

drivers.explanation: Growth across all segments from new program starts and execution against record backlog; higher ISR, classified space, F-35, and international communications volumes contributed.
Gross profit growth is explained by revenue growth (+8.4% y/y) outpacing cost-of-revenue growth (+7.0% y/y), consistent with the segment-level margin commentary.
Higher Communications & Spectrum Dominance segment income and lower corporate/other expense drove the gain, partly offset by the absence of a 2025 $92M asset-sale gain and higher R&D.
EBIT growth outpaces the $83M operating-income increase because non-service FAS pension income rose to $185M from $105M, adding to the operating gain.
EPS rose on higher volume, improved program performance, and lower corporate expense, including the non-cash preferred stock deemed dividend; partly offset by lower net asset and investment gains.
Cash rose mainly on a $973M net-proceeds inflow from a subsidiary Series A preferred stock issuance (financing activities) plus higher operating cash flow of $879M, up 37% y/y.

Decline y/y is consistent with debt repayments recorded across trailing quarters; current portion of long-term debt rose to $1.815B from $673M at FY2025 year-end, indicating near-term maturities were reclassified out of long-term.
CEO cites the 'Trusted Disruptor' culture and execution against a record $42B backlog; orders of $7.3B and a 1.2x book-to-bill reinforce a multi-year growth track record.
